prompt: Where does the `context` package's documentation say a context goes in a function's signature?
hint: `go doc context` printed the convention with an example.

choices.text: Last, after the arguments it qualifies
choices.why: The documented convention is the opposite end: first.

choices.text: The first parameter, named `ctx` by convention
choices.why: Right: `func DoSomething(ctx context.Context, arg Arg) error`.

choices.text: In a field of the struct the method belongs to
choices.why: That is the thing the documentation says not to do.

choices.text: In a package-level variable set once in `main`
choices.why: A package variable would be shared by every request; a context belongs to one call.

prompt: In `layers.go`, `report` never calls `ctx.Done()` or `ctx.Err()`. Why did it still stop when the 150 milliseconds ran out?
hint: What did `report` do with `ctx`, and what did the function below it do?

choices.text: The runtime stops every function of a goroutine whose context ended
choices.why: The runtime stops nothing. Only code that looks at the context reacts to it.

choices.text: It handed `ctx` to `fetch`
choices.why: Right. Passing `ctx` down was all the middle layer had to do.

choices.text: `WithTimeout` panics in every function below it
choices.why: No panic happened: the program printed an error and exited normally.

choices.text: `report` had its own timer of 150 ms
choices.why: Only `handle` set a deadline; `report` mentions no time at all.

prompt: The error from `layers.go` was `report for ana: fetch mar: context deadline exceeded`. What let `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` still answer `true`?
hint: Look at the verb in the two `fmt.Errorf` calls.

choices.text: The string contains the words "deadline exceeded"
choices.why: `errors.Is` never compares text; it walks the chain of wrapped errors.

choices.text: `context.DeadlineExceeded` matches any error
choices.why: It matches only itself, found somewhere in the chain.

choices.text: Each layer wrapped the error it received using `%w`
choices.why: Right. `%w` keeps the original reachable for `errors.Is`, as lesson 34 of `go` showed.

choices.text: `fetch` returned `ctx.Err()` with no wrapping at all
choices.why: `fetch` did wrap it, as `fetch mar: …`; the wrapping with `%w` is why it still matched.

prompt: A team keeps the context of the request that built their `Client` in a field, and uses it for every later call. What goes wrong?
hint: Who owns that context, and how long does it live?

choices.text: Nothing, as long as the field is unexported
choices.why: Visibility is not the problem; the lifetime of the context is.

choices.text: It belongs to a finished request
choices.why: Right. The struct outlives the call, so its context belongs to somebody else's request.

choices.text: The compiler refuses a field of type `context.Context`
choices.why: It compiles; the rule is a convention, which is why it has to be learnt.

choices.text: Each call gets a fresh deadline from that field
choices.why: A context's deadline is fixed when it is made; nothing in it renews.

prompt: In `tree.go`, `child` asked for one second but its parent `root` had 100 milliseconds. When did `child` end?
hint: The last line of the output.

choices.text: At 100 ms, with root's deadline
choices.why: Right: `child done after 100ms`. A child's deadline is the earlier of its own and its parent's.

choices.text: At one second, as it asked
choices.why: A child cannot outlive its parent; it reported root's deadline as its own.

choices.text: At 1.1 s, adding both timeouts
choices.why: Timeouts do not add. The earlier deadline wins.

choices.text: Straight away, when `sibling` was cancelled
choices.why: Right after that cancel, `child` still answered `<nil>`.

prompt: `sibling` was derived from `root` and cancelled by hand. Which were still running straight afterwards? Choose all that apply.
hint: An end travels down the tree.

choices.text: `root`
choices.why: Yes: `root: <nil>`. Cancelling a child does not touch its parent.

choices.text: `child`
choices.why: Yes: `child: <nil>`. Siblings are independent.

choices.text: `sibling`
choices.why: It was the one cancelled: `context canceled`.

choices.text: A context derived from `sibling`
choices.why: Anything derived from `sibling` ends with it.

prompt: A derived context comes with a function that ends it, and the line straight after deriving it is `defer ___()`.
hint: The name `tree.go` and `layers.go` gave that function.

prompt: What does `go vet` report about `ctx, _ := context.WithTimeout(parent, time.Second)`?
hint: What happens to a child nobody cancels?

choices.text: That one second is too long for a timeout
choices.why: `vet` has no opinion on durations.

choices.text: That `parent` might be `nil`
choices.why: That is a separate rule of the documentation, and not what `vet` reports here.

choices.text: Nothing, since the deadline ends the child anyway
choices.why: It does report it, because until then the child's bookkeeping is held for nothing.

choices.text: The discarded cancel function leaks the context
choices.why: Right: `the cancel function returned by context.WithTimeout should be called, not discarded`.

prompt: In `detach.go`, `stop()` returned `false`. What did that mean?

choices.text: That `AfterFunc` failed to register the function
choices.why: It registered it and ran it: its line was the first one printed.

choices.text: It came too late: the function had already run
choices.why: Right. `stop` returns true only if it prevented the call.

choices.text: That the context had not been cancelled yet
choices.why: `ctx` reported `context canceled`.

choices.text: That `WithoutCancel` had switched `AfterFunc` off
choices.why: `WithoutCancel` made a new context, `audit`; the original `ctx` and its `AfterFunc` were untouched.

prompt: A handler must write an audit record even when the client hangs up mid-request, and the record should carry the request's id. Which context does the write get?
hint: It needs the values and not the ending.

choices.text: The request's context, unchanged
choices.why: That one ends when the client hangs up, and the write would be cancelled with it.

choices.text: `context.Background()`
choices.why: It never ends, but it has none of the request's values, so the id is lost.

choices.text: `context.WithoutCancel` applied to the request's context
choices.why: Right: the values stay, as `audit` kept `req-7f3a`, and the ending does not reach it.

choices.text: A child made with `context.WithTimeout` of a minute
choices.why: A child ends when its parent does, so the hang-up still cancels it.

prompt: `polite` in `loop.go` checks `ctx.Err()` before each item. How many of the 300 items did it finish before the 50 ms deadline stopped it?
hint: The second line of the output.

prompt: `deaf` was handed a context with a 50 ms deadline and returned after 350 ms. What does that say about cancellation?
hint: What did `deaf` do with its `ctx` parameter?

choices.text: A context stops nothing by itself; the work has to look
choices.why: Right. `deaf` accepted `ctx` and never consulted it.

choices.text: The deadline was too short for the scheduler to deliver
choices.why: `polite` got the same deadline and stopped at 50 ms.

choices.text: `time.Sleep` blocks cancellation inside a goroutine
choices.why: `polite` sleeps the same millisecond per item and stopped on time.

choices.text: The context was cancelled at 350 ms, not 50
choices.why: It ended at 50 ms; nothing read it until the loop was over.

prompt: A loop waits on each turn for a value from a channel, `v := <-results`. Why is checking `ctx.Err()` at the top of the loop not enough?
hint: Where does the loop spend its time?

choices.text: `ctx.Err()` is not safe to call from inside a loop like this one
choices.why: It is safe from any goroutine, as `polite` showed.

choices.text: It sits blocked in the receive, where no check runs
choices.why: Right. The check has to happen during the wait, which only a `select` can do.

choices.text: Channels ignore contexts until they are closed
choices.why: A channel knows nothing about contexts either way; the question is what the loop waits on.

choices.text: `ctx.Err()` returns `nil` until the loop ends
choices.why: It returns the reason as soon as the context has ended.

prompt: A loop of very fast steps, each a few nanoseconds, gets a context. What does the lesson recommend?
hint: The rule is about time, not counts.

choices.text: Check before every step, exactly like `polite`
choices.why: It works, but a check on every one of a billion tiny steps buys nothing: the overrun would be nanoseconds either way.

choices.text: Skip the check, because fast loops finish anyway
choices.why: A billion fast steps still take seconds; the loop must look sometimes.

choices.text: Check every so many steps
choices.why: Right: look often enough that the loop overruns by an amount nobody minds, every thousand for instance.

choices.text: Run it in a separate goroutine that the context kills
choices.why: Nothing kills a goroutine from outside; it has to return by itself.

prompt: Put the roles of the three layers in `layers.go` in order, from where the request arrives to where it waits.
items: `handle` derives a context with a 150 ms timeout
`fetch` waits on the slow call or on `ctx.Done()`

prompt: Match each function with what it is for.
hint: Two of them sit at the edges of a request.

pairs.right: run cleanup once a context ends
keep the values, drop the ending
mark where a context is still missing
give part of the work a shorter limit

right_distractors: make a child live longer than its parent

prompt: A function receives a context that has already been cancelled, and its first act would be to open a file and start three goroutines. What should it do?

choices.text: Start the goroutines and let each notice the cancellation
choices.why: It would open a file and start work whose answer nobody is waiting for.

choices.text: Return the context's error at once, before opening anything
choices.why: Right: check before starting expensive work at all.

choices.text: Derive a fresh context with `WithoutCancel` and carry on
choices.why: That ignores the caller's decision, which is the misuse section 03 warned about.

choices.text: Panic, since a cancelled context is a programming error
choices.why: A cancelled context is ordinary: a client left, a deadline passed. It is answered with an error.
